To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the refractive index profiles of optical fibers can be rapidly determined, with high accuracy and precision, in a nondestructive manner, by measuring the interference fringes produced when a single-pass interference optical microscope is used to illuminate the fiber transversely to the fiber axis and to collect the scattered light from the fiber.

the refractive index of a single-mode fiber can be rapidly determined to within approximately 1 percent by measuring the intensity distribution of the interference pattern produced by the fiber when it is immersed in index matching oil and illuminated transverse to its axis.

a fiber’s index profile can be determined automatically and accurately by measuring the interference pattern produced when a single pass of light is reflected from the fiber’s surface and that this technique can be used to measure profiles of fibers as short as 0.1 mm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of nondestructive methods for the automatic measurement of the index profile of a fiber.
the development of nondestructive methods for the rapid determination of the index distribution in optical fibers.

the development of automatic, nondestructive optical methods for measuring the index profile of a glass fiber, for determining the fiber's mode structure, and for characterizing the optical properties of the fiber.
